newsitem.title: UK: Stolt predicts parcel tanker rates will stay firm.
newsitem.headline: Stolt predicts parcel tanker rates will stay firm.

text.p: Stolt Parcel Tankers said on Tuesday the company expected improved spot rates for chemical carriers to continue throughout the rest of the year.

Stolt Tank Containers managing director Reginald Lee told a Stolt-Nielsen SA group shareholders' meeting: "Over the last four to five months spot rates for parcel tankers have improved. We do not see much further change over the rest of the year."

Earlier the group had said the large number of ships which entered the trade in 1996, equivalent to about six percent of the world fleet of parcel tankers, had caused disruption despite continuing growth in demand.
"We expect the current supply/demand balance to remain stable for the remainder of the year," Stolt-Nielsen said on April 9 when reporting its first quarter results for 1997.
Lee added: "We expect supply and demand to keep a nice balance over the next three to four years."

The company says market research is predicting demand for the transportation of petrochemicals to grow in excess of five percent a year through to 1999 while ship supply will increase by around four percent a year from 1997 to 1999.
Stolt-Nielsen said that in 1996 it had a 21 percent share of the world parcel tankers fleet - only matched by Odfjell of Norway with the same market share.

By 1999, when it has taken delivery of a further 20 vessels it has on order, but also scrapped 13 older ships, Stolt-Nielsen predicted it would hold a 23 percent share of the world fleet and that Odfjell would have fallen back to a 20 percent ownership.

Stolt-Nielsen added that its ship orders represented about a third of the order book for parcel tankers being delivered over the next three years. -- Paul Berrill, Reuters Shipping News +44 171 452 4087
